passages.title: The History of the Bicycle
passages.text: The bicycle has undergone remarkable transformation since its earliest wooden prototypes appeared in the nineteenth century, evolving from a novelty for the wealthy into one of the most widely used vehicles on Earth. Aluminium frames are prized today for being significantly lighter than traditional steel frames, which improved both speed and portability. The earliest wooden 'draisine' bicycle was introduced around 1817. Pedals were first attached to the front wheel in 1861. The 'penny-farthing' design featured a dramatically larger front wheel. The invention of the pneumatic tyre in 1888 greatly improved comfort. Mass production techniques reduced the average price by roughly 50 percent within a decade. Modern racing bicycles now use frames commonly made from aluminium. The safety bicycle, with two similarly sized wheels, became popular mainly because it was far easier to balance and ride than the penny-farthing. Bicycle use declined sharply in many wealthy countries after the mass availability of affordable cars in the mid-twentieth century. The earliest wooden draisine relied on the rider pushing along the ground with their feet, since it had no pedals at all. Its large front wheel made the penny-farthing notoriously difficult and even dangerous for beginners to mount and ride. Mass production techniques reduced the average price by roughly 50 percent within a decade. Modern racing bicycles now use frames commonly made from aluminium. Aluminium frames are prized today for being significantly lighter than traditional steel frames, which improved both speed and portability.

passages.title: Microplastics in Freshwater Systems
passages.text: While ocean plastic pollution has attracted global attention, scientists are increasingly concerned about microplastic contamination in rivers and lakes, which supply drinking water to billions of people. Microplastics are generally defined as particles smaller than 5 millimetres. A recent survey sampled 60 river sites across the region. The most common source identified was fibres from synthetic clothing. Filtration upgrades at treatment plants removed up to 90 percent of particles. Researchers used a 300 micron mesh to collect samples. The study was funded by a national research council. One recommendation was to install filters in domestic washing machines. The survey's main aim was to map the sources and concentration of microplastic contamination across freshwater systems. Even with upgrades, treatment plants remain only partially effective, since some particles are too small to be filtered out entirely. Reducing pollution at the source, the researchers argue, would require changes to clothing design and washing habits rather than relying on treatment plants alone. While ocean plastic pollution has attracted global attention, scientists are increasingly concerned about microplastic contamination in rivers and lakes. Filtration upgrades at treatment plants removed up to 90 percent of particles. The most common source identified was fibres from synthetic clothing. Rivers and lakes supply drinking water to billions of people, and the study's concern was precisely that this contamination reaches those supplies.

The term 'attention economy' was popularised in the 1990s. Some platforms now report daily active users to investors every three months. A design feature called infinite scroll was introduced to reduce natural stopping points. questions.prompt: The table below shows average weekly hours spent on three leisure activities by adults in a single country in 2000 and 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
questions.modelAnswer:
The table compares the average weekly hours adults spent on three leisure activities in 2000 and 2023. Overall, time spent online rose dramatically, while both television viewing and reading declined over the period.

In 2000, watching television was by far the most popular activity, taking up twelve hours a week, more than twice the time spent reading and six times that spent online. By 2023, this pattern had reversed almost entirely: online activities had grown sevenfold to fourteen hours a week, overtaking television, which fell to just seven hours. Reading also decreased, though less sharply, from five hours to three.

Overall, the data reveal a clear shift in leisure habits, with online activity replacing television as the dominant use of adults' free time, while traditional reading continued a slower decline.

questions.prompt: Some people believe that children should begin learning a foreign language as early as possible, while others think it is better to wait until secondary school. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Write at least 250 words.
questions.modelAnswer:
The question of when children should start learning a foreign language divides educators and parents alike, and both early and later approaches have credible support.

Those who favour an early start point to research suggesting that young children acquire new sounds and grammar more naturally than older learners, since their brains are especially adaptable during early childhood. Early exposure can also build confidence, as young children are typically less self-conscious about making mistakes than teenagers.

On the other hand, supporters of a later start argue that secondary school students can draw on stronger literacy skills in their first language, which helps them understand grammar rules more quickly. They also note that younger children have limited attention spans, so structured language lessons may be less effective than informal exposure through songs or games.

In my view, an early start is preferable, provided the teaching method suits young learners. Rather than formal grammar instruction, primary schools should use songs, stories and games to build familiarity with a language, reserving more structured grammar teaching for secondary school. This combined approach captures the cognitive advantages of an early start while respecting how young children actually learn best.

In conclusion, while both early and later introductions to language learning have merit, I believe an early, play-based start followed by more formal study later offers the best balance for most children.
